meta.title: Corporate Tambola use-case oracle: join, verify, approval, people permissions

boundTo.head: 09d6696
boundTo.note: The working tree was being edited while this was written (the 'ended' and 'locked' gates and the 'admitted' override appeared during the work). Re-run docs/flow/04-count-cases.mjs --check against a live worker before relying on a row; every row of the main join table was checked against the real Worker (see validation).

meta.howToUse: Pure function. For one case (an object with the dimension values) first derive the audience flags and the route owner (derive), then walk the ordered rules of the family (join.rules, approval.rules, input.defects, perm.rules); the first rule whose 'when' matches gives the answer. 'when' keys are ANDed; an array value means 'any of'; {not: v} means 'not v'. Keys are dimension names or derived names (closed, employeesOnly, invites, owner, limited, inChain, role, caller, op).
meta.answerShape: {status, code ('ticket' for a 200 with a pid), waiting, with, sees, final, msg (key into messages; {with},{limit},{cap} are filled in)}

playMode.note: manual = a Host presses a button for each number (config callMode:'host', needs cap <= 2000); auto = the software calls at the chosen speed. The Worker never reads callMode in the join, people or waiting routes (worker.ts join route, people.ts), so this dimension is a REPLICATE axis: every case must give the same answer in both modes.

verify.note: config.verify. 'mobile' is stored as no value (default).

EMP_ONLY.label: Employees only
EMP_ONLY.settings: whoCanJoin list (forced), employeesOnly true, guestInvites off (forced by config.ts:332)

LIST.label: A list of people I choose (closed list, no guest invites)
LIST.settings: whoCanJoin list, employeesOnly false, guestInvites off

LIST_INV.label: A list plus the people they invite (closed list, guest invites on)
LIST_INV.settings: whoCanJoin list, employeesOnly false, guestInvites on (per 1..10, default 4). With verify id/either/both this is the nearest server setting to console choice 2 'My employees, plus their friends and family' (see doubtful row DR-18)

ANYONE.label: Anyone with the link
ANYONE.settings: whoCanJoin anyone, employeesOnly false, guestInvites off

EMP_ID_OTHERS.label: Anyone with the link; employees confirm with their employee ID, others use a mobile number
EMP_ID_OTHERS.settings: whoCanJoin anyone, employeesOnly false, verify id|either|both

ANYONE_INV.label: EXTENSION: Anyone with the link, guest invites on
ANYONE_INV.settings: whoCanJoin anyone, guestInvites on. Not offered as a console choice but the server allows it, and it is the only audience where a level-1 guest's quota is hit in an OPEN game (the 'over by invite' capacity).

route.HOST: Host common link: from = 1500000000 + hex(first 7 of the Host key hash)
route.COHOST: Co-host common link: from = 1000000000 + hex(first 7 of the Co-host key hash)
route.PERSONAL: Personal link /j/<token>: a secret made for one listed person (fixture convention: the person is on a Co-host's list). The page sends {token}.
route.GUEST_L1: Guest invite link of a level-1 participant (a participant who is not themself a guest): from = that participant's seat number
route.GUEST_L2: Guest invite link of a level-2 guest (somebody who joined through a level-1 guest's link or list): same shape, but the game ignores it for ownership
route.DIRECT: No link code: the bare game page (z.html?e=ID) or a typed address

state.S01: On a list with a mobile number only
state.S02: On a list with an employee ID only (no mobile)
state.S03: On a list with both a mobile number and an employee ID
state.S04: Not on any list (an outsider): types only a mobile number; on a PERSONAL route types their own number on somebody else's link
state.S05: Removed by the organizer side before the game (before start): was listed, now status removed
state.S06: Already joined on another phone: the identity holds a ticket bound to device A, the request comes from device B (another phone, another browser, cleared site data)
state.S07: Same phone, second ticket: the request's device already holds a ticket for a DIFFERENT identity
state.S08: Wrong ID: an employee ID that matches nobody (in 'both' mode: a listed mobile with an ID different from the listed one)
state.S09: ID of someone else who already joined (in 'both' mode: the person's own unlisted mobile with that other person's ID)
state.S10: ID of someone else who is listed but has NOT joined yet (impersonation window)
state.S11: Returning: same identity, same device, second visit (reload, reopen the link)

capacity.ROOM: Room left for this person (a free place, no promise problem, inviter quota not reached)
capacity.PROMISED_ONLY: The only free places are promised to listed people who have not yet joined: participants + unseated listed people == cap, participants < cap
capacity.FULL: Exactly full: participants == cap (the next new ticket would exceed the size bought)
capacity.OVER_QUOTA: The game has room, but the person's inviter (a Co-host with 100 default, or a level-1 guest with 'per') has no list places left

lifecycle.pause_resume: The organizer pauses and later resumes the numbers; the step under test happens while paused (signed control file only: nothing in join, people or waiting reads it) - REPLICATE of 'none'
lifecycle.late_join: The step happens after the first number and after the 2-minute grace (40 rounds): new seats get jr = the current round
lifecycle.organizer_ends: The step happens after the game ended (last call + 60 s, or the organizer's stop): endBoundMs. Since commit 5d51d94 a join is NOT refused after the end (the page shows the thank-you and share page by design); the waiting room, list adds and decisions ARE refused as lapsed.
lifecycle.cancelled_before_start: The step happens after the Organizer or a Host cancelled the game (3 confirmations). Co-host keys are revoked at the cancel.
lifecycle.reopen: A cancelled PAID game moved to a new date: cancelled flag cleared, Co-host keys stay revoked, guest data is gone (erased 20 h after the cancel): nobody has joined, old personal links are dead, old guest links point at no seat. The Organizer has loaded the lists again (new personal links).

approval.AUTO: No waiting room: the join itself gives the ticket (auto-admit)
approval.APPROVE: waiting-room approve (single request) by a right approver
approval.APPROVE_ALL: 'Approve all' by a right approver (only their own link's requests for a Co-host or guest)
approval.APPROVE_AFTER_FULL: approve after all places on the lists are taken (persons == cap)
approval.APPROVE_AFTER_REMOVAL: approve after the same identity was listed and then removed
approval.WRONG_ROLE: approve by a role that may not decide this request
approval.NONE: the join ended in an error, so there is nothing to approve

approverRole.COHOST_OWNER: the Co-host whose common link the request came through
approverRole.COHOST_OTHER: a Co-host who does not own the request
approverRole.L1_OWNER: the level-1 guest whose invite link the request came through (known by ticket id + device)
approverRole.AI_KEY: an AI key or any call through an AI work link

derive.fromAudience: closed, employeesOnly and invites come from dimensions.audience[audience]. 'employeesOnly' is also called eo.

ownerRules.note: Co-host keys are revoked at the cancel and not restored by the reopen: the link silently credits the organizer
seat numbers start again from 1 after the erase and nobody has joined yet, so the old guest link points at no seat (DR-24: later it may point at a different person)
guest invitations are off: the link is ignored
a level-2 guest's link records no inviter; no link at all = the organizer
fixture convention: the link belongs to a person on a Co-host's list; a different number typed on it asks that list's owner

derive.limited: owner is 'c' (Co-host: coHostLimit, default 100, 10..1000) or 's' (level-1 guest: invites.per, default 4, 1..10)
derive.holdsListPlace: true when the subject (or, on route PERSONAL, the link holder) already has a place on a list: states S01, S02, S03, S10 (the adopted listed person), S08 in verify both (the subject's mobile is listed), and every PERSONAL case. Such a person cannot meet a full game: lists may not exceed the size and the size cannot be set below the listed people.

labelOfOwner.h: <the label the Organizer gave the Host, else 'the host'>
labelOfOwner.c: <the label the Organizer gave the Co-host, else 'the co-host'>

derive.listedOwner: The list owner of a listed person: 'c' on route PERSONAL (fixture), otherwise 'o' (the Organizer loaded the list). First list wins: a listed person stays under their real inviter whatever link they use.
derive.seatInv: the level-1 seat number when the inviter is 's', otherwise null

recipes.common: Every request carries consent {v: current Terms version, boxes: [A,B]} and a device id (16..64 hex). Unless a case says otherwise the person is on its own phone with a fresh device id.
recipes.identities: S = the subject: mobile M_s, employee ID E_s, device D_s. O = another listed person: M_o, E_o, device D_o. Wrong ID = an ID that is on no list.
recipes.listedBy: the Organizer for every route except PERSONAL; the Co-host for PERSONAL (the token is the personal link of that list entry)

S04.request: {phone: M_s}   (PERSONAL: {token: of a listed person X, phone: M_s})

S05.list: same kind as the verify mode needs (mobile: mobileOnly, id|either: idOnly, both: both), then the Organizer removes the person before the start

S06.list: as S05 without the removal; the person first joins with device A
S06.request: the same request with device B

S07.list: as S05 without the removal; a different listed person 'holder' first joins with device D_s
S07.request: the subject's own request with device D_s

S08.list: mode both: the subject's mobile is listed with ID E_s; modes id|either: somebody else is listed
S08.request: mode both: {phone: M_s, empId: <wrong>}; id|either: {empId: <wrong>}; PERSONAL: {token, empId: <wrong>}

S09.list: O is listed and has joined on D_o
S09.request: id|either: {empId: E_o}; both: {phone: M_s (unlisted), empId: E_o}; PERSONAL: {token, empId: E_o}

S10.list: O is listed and has NOT joined

S11.list: as S05 without the removal; the person joined with device D_s
S11.request: the same request again with D_s

verifyKindForListing.either: mobileOnly (for the PERSONAL token holder) / idOnly (for S05..S10 ID cases)

routeParams.PERSONAL: token = last path part of the person's /j/<token> link
routeParams.GUEST_L1: from = seat number of a level-1 participant
routeParams.GUEST_L2: from = seat number of a level-2 guest

recipes.anchors: Worlds are built with three anchors while guest invitations are on, then switched to the audience's final settings: A1 = level-1 participant (listed by the Organizer, joined), A2 = level-2 guest (came through A1's link, admitted, joined), A3 = a second level-1 participant. Also: one Host, two Co-hosts (the second is the 'other' Co-host), another organizer's key, an AI key.

capacityFixtures.FULL: fillers are listed and join until participants == persons; then PATCH cap to that number. A subject who holds a list place cannot be present (the lists may not exceed the size, and since commit 1b45d5e the size cannot be set below the listed people), so FULL is crossed only with subjects who hold no list place
capacityFixtures.PROMISED_ONLY: list K extra people who do not join, then PATCH cap = participants + unseated listed people
capacityFixtures.OVER_QUOTA: Co-host: coHostLimit 10 with 10 people on the Co-host's list; level-1 guest: invites.per 1 with the anchor level-2 guest already on A1's list

lifecycleFixtures.pause_resume: no fixture needed (pause is a signed file nobody reads in join/people)
lifecycleFixtures.late_join: now = start + 4 minutes (after the 2-minute grace, before the end); the game is paid (pack > 0) so it is not 'locked'
lifecycleFixtures.reopen: cancel, delete the guest rows (person, waiting, seat, participant), clear the cancel mark, load the subject's list entry (and for S10 the other person's) again by the Organizer (new tokens). Emulated in the probe: a real reopen needs a paid game and a payment.

pruning.rule: audience x verify: only the 'verifyAllowed' values of each audience are crossed (ANYONE and ANYONE_INV: mobile only; EMP_ID_OTHERS: id, either, both - with 'mobile' it would be the ANYONE audience).
pruning.why: An open game with verify 'mobile' and an employee-ID rule is a contradiction in terms; the same server setting is already covered by ANYONE.

pruning.rule: state validity by verify mode (table stateInvalidWhen).
pruning.why: A person cannot be listed in a shape the people route refuses (people.ts addPeople): ID-only needs id|either; mobile-only needs not(eo && id|both); an ID is never stored in 'mobile' mode; S10 cannot exist in 'both' (identity is the mobile, so an unclaimed ID is the same as S09).

pruning.rule: lifecycle reopen: states S05, S06, S07, S09, S11 do not exist, and capacity is ROOM only.
pruning.why: A reopened game starts empty: guest data was erased 20 h after the cancel, so nobody has been removed and nobody holds a ticket or a device yet. Capacity checks are the same code as in a game that was never cancelled, so FULL, PROMISED_ONLY and OVER_QUOTA add nothing there.

pruning.rule: capacity values are kept for a case only if the rule that answers the case lists that capacity (rule.capacities, default ROOM only). FULL additionally needs holdsListPlace = false.
pruning.why: A case whose answer is decided by a gate before the capacity check (need-id, link-gone, returning phone, device-used, ended, cancelled) cannot depend on capacity, so FULL/PROMISED_ONLY/OVER_QUOTA there are the same use case as ROOM. OVER_QUOTA needs an inviter that has a quota (limited) and an unlisted person. FULL cannot meet a person who holds a list place: the lists never exceed the size, and since commit 1b45d5e the size cannot be set below the people on the lists, so a game is full only when everyone on the lists has come in.

pruning.rule: rules marked 'ignores' keep one case per combination of the OTHER dimensions (the first value in enumeration order stands for the ignored ones).
pruning.why: The cancelled gate answers 403 before verify, state and capacity are read; a dead personal link after a reopen answers 404 before them; and so on. Keeping every verify x state there would only repeat one use case.

pruning.rule: Approval outcomes other than AUTO and NONE exist only for requests that the join oracle answers with waiting:true.
Approver roles: APPROVE, APPROVE_ALL, DECLINE, APPROVE_AFTER_FULL, APPROVE_AFTER_REMOVAL cross only the RIGHT roles of the request; WRONG_ROLE crosses the six wrong roles; NEVER crosses no role.
pruning.why: A right role approving is one use case; a wrong role is the refusal use case.

pruning.rule: Family F-INPUT crosses defects with (audience x verify) only; family F-PERM crosses caller x op x invites x lifecycle with the 'ignores' of its rules.
pruning.why: A malformed field is refused before route, state, capacity and lifecycle matter.

pruning.rule: F-APPROVAL requests are one per (audience, route, request class, identity kind): request class is 'unlisted' (S04) or 'idmiss' (S08, S09, S10); identity kind is 'id' when the waiting request is keyed by a typed employee ID (verify id|either) and 'phone' otherwise. The approver's answer does not depend on verify or on which of S08/S09/S10 produced the request.
pruning.why: approval.rules read only the request's owner, whether it is overlimit, and the audience's invite switch. Crossing every verify and state again would repeat identical answers.

pruning.rule: F-APPROVAL is a base plus a sweep. Base (decision lifecycle none): every approval outcome x its roles x its capacity. Sweep (decision lifecycle pause_resume, late_join, organizer_ends, cancelled_before_start; reopen only for Co-host-link requests): APPROVE by every right role, NEVER, and for organizer_ends and cancelled_before_start also the two non-chain wrong roles.
pruning.why: The game-state gates (cancelled, ended) and the dead Co-host keys change the approver's answer; pause and late join only change the re-join leg. Crossing all five lifecycles with every outcome would repeat the base answers.

pruning.rule: F-APPROVAL: a request whose identity already has a person row (state S08 in verify both: the subject's mobile is listed, only the typed ID was wrong) is not crossed with APPROVE_AFTER_FULL, APPROVE_AFTER_REMOVAL, or APPROVE_ALL at OVER_QUOTA.
pruning.why: Admitting changes nothing for a person who is already on a list, so the cap check, the removal order and the all-approve quota path do not apply (single APPROVE still refuses over-limit: DR-25).

pruning.rule: playMode is crossed with every family and never pruned.
pruning.why: It is a replicate axis: the oracle is identical, so each manual case must equal its auto twin (a cheap invariance check).

join.note: F-JOIN: one join request (and for waiting results the first leg of the waiting room). 'capacities' lists the capacity values for which the rule is a distinct, meaningful case (default ROOM only). 'ignores' lists dimensions that do not influence the answer of the rule (see PR-05).

personByToken: guest data was erased, the old token no longer exists
worker.ts join: token unknown or person removed (a removal also clears tok_hash)
worker.ts join: employeesOnly && id && no ID && no token
worker.ts join: employeesOnly && both && no ID && no token
worker.ts join: have participant, same device (again:true)
worker.ts join: token && !typedPh
worker.ts join: idHit
worker.ts join: device mismatch
the typed ID resolves to a listed person who already holds a ticket on another device
worker.ts join: person status removed
worker.ts join: a seat already holds this device
worker.ts join: participants >= cap (no code; checked BEFORE the waiting room, so 'full' beats 'waiting')
worker.ts join: person found on a list; the promised place is kept (addSeat)

then.note: the token is the strong proof: a typed ID is ignored

rules.src: worker.ts join: ID checks are skipped when a token is present
worker.ts join: a listed ID is accepted from any phone that has not joined yet

then.note: ID mismatch: the organizer decides, in open and closed games alike (doubtful DR-02)

rules.src: worker.ts join: idMiss -> wait(false)
worker.ts join: e.closed -> wait(false)
worker.ts join: listCount(owner) >= limit -> wait(true, limit)
worker.ts join: the insert guard fails -> row null -> guardId !== null -> wait(true, guardLimit)
worker.ts join: the insert guard fails -> row null -> 409 full
worker.ts join: open game, inviter below its limit

finals.nothing: no row is created; the phone has no ticket and no waiting request
finals.new-ticket: participant + seat created. person row: status joined; inviter = placement (listedOwner: the list the person was on; owner: the route owner); seat.inv = level-1 seat number when the inviter is 's' else null; seat.src = co:<hex> | ho:<hex> | link; jr = 0 normally, the current round when lifecycle late_join
finals.same-ticket: no new row; the reply carries again:true and the original jr
finals.waiting-row: waiting row created (status waiting, one per identity, idempotent): inviter = owner (or 'o' when overlimit), overlimit flag, via = personal-link | common-link | direct, chain = the owner and, for 's', the guest's own inviter; NO seat, NO person row; the request is visible to 'sees'

approval.note: F-APPROVAL: a request already exists (the waiting answer of a join case); the step under test is a decision by 'role' under 'lifecycle' with 'capacity'. Rules are evaluated top to bottom; inChain is derived (see derivation).

derivation.rightRoles: ORG and HOST always. COHOST_OWNER when the request's owner is 'c' and the request is not overlimit and the Co-host key is alive (not lifecycle cancelled_before_start, not reopen). L1_OWNER when the owner is 's', not overlimit, and guest invites are on. An overlimit request (open game, inviter list full) is on chain ',o,': only ORG and HOST.
derivation.inChain: role in {ORG, HOST} or (role COHOST_OWNER and owner c and not overlimit) or (role L1_OWNER and owner s and not overlimit). COHOST_OTHER and L1_OTHER are never in the chain. (If the level-1 guest was themself put on a Co-host's list, that Co-host is also in the chain of the guest's requests: the fixture lists the anchor guest under the Organizer to avoid it.)
derivation.requestKinds: Every JOIN case whose oracle result has waiting:true is a request: (audience, verify, route, state, capacity ROOM) = ordinary waiting request; (…, capacity OVER_QUOTA) in an open game = overlimit request (chain ',o,').
derivation.placedUnder: request.overlimit -> the approver's own label (Organizer / Host <label>); else if capacity OVER_QUOTA and the approver is ORG or HOST -> the approver's own label; else the request owner's label (Organizer / Host <label> / Co-host <label> / Guest (ticket n)).
derivation.decisionCapacity: APPROVE, APPROVE_ALL, DECLINE: ROOM or OVER_QUOTA (the target list is full; only when the owner is c or s and the request is not overlimit). APPROVE_AFTER_FULL: FULL. Others: ROOM.
derivation.decisionLifecycle: The request is created at baseline (lifecycle none, or reopen for the reopen cases). The decision happens in the stated lifecycle.
derivation.afterApprove: me?wid -> admitted; the phone re-sends the same join -> 200 ticket; person.inviter = placedUnder id, status joined; seat.inv = the level-1 seat when placed under 's'.

then.note: no call is made; the phone keeps polling; at the end me says lapsed

rules.note: the cancel revoked every Co-host key of the game, and the reopen did not give them back (DR-14)
a Co-host or level-1 guest outside the request's chain is told the request does not exist (APPROVE_ALL answers 200 with zeros instead, see doubtful DR-15)
listing the waiting person admits the request at once; the later removal wins and Admit changes nothing. The 'already' answer comes BEFORE the game-ended check.

approval.approveAllNote: APPROVE_ALL by a Co-host or level-1 guest outside the chain returns 200 {admitted:0, declined:0, stillWaiting:0} (not 404): the list is filtered by chain, so nothing matches.

input.note: F-INPUT: one malformed or incomplete join request. Profiles name the verify mode and employees-only. 'continue' means the request is a normal S04 (outsider) request and the join rules answer it. Error answers have no 'code' when the code column is null.

perm.note: Lifecycle 'none' = before the start, 'late_join' = started, 'organizer_ends' = ended. GET routes (LIST, EXPORT, WAITING_LIST) are never blocked by a cancel; every write is.

rules.note: the cancel revoked the Co-host key

doubtful.title: Any phone can take a listed colleague's place by typing their employee ID
doubtful.rows: J-IMPERSONATE (state S10; verify id|either; every audience)
doubtful.where: apps/edge/src/worker.ts:1603-1607 (the ID is looked up first and the listed person is adopted); 1650-1656 (only MISSES are throttled)
doubtful.why: A listed ID that has not been used yet is treated as proof of identity: the first phone that types it gets the ticket, in an employees-only game too, and the real employee later gets 423 id-used (rule J-ID-USED-S09). An employee ID is not a secret, and a correct guess is never counted or limited. The people spec says a typed number is only 'matched, not proven'; for IDs nobody asked the organizer.

doubtful.title: An outsider (or a typo) in an OPEN game is parked in the waiting room with a message that is wrong for open games
doubtful.rows: J-ID-MISS-WAIT (S08, S09 in 'both'; audience EMP_ID_OTHERS, and every closed audience)
doubtful.where: apps/edge/src/worker.ts:1649 (idMiss = true), 1699 (if (e.closed || idMiss) return wait(false, null))
doubtful.why: In an open 'employees by ID, others by mobile' game anybody who types an ID that is on no list waits for approval and is told 'This engagement is by invitation', although the game is open and the console tells the organizer 'you do not need to approve anyone'. Every mistyped ID is a new waiting row (500 rows block everybody: waiting-full). Same as docs G9.

doubtful.title: Admitting a request that carried someone else's ID creates a second person with the same employee ID
